notes:
A three-rung Abyssea repeatable, and both key items are real evidence, which is unusual for this family. The unnumbered line above bullet 1 -- only one Ward Warden / Desert Rain / Crimson Carpet quest per Vana'dielian day, across ALL Abyssea areas -- is a cooldown, not a step, and nothing in the packets reports it.

Bullets 2, 3 and 4 are one step. Bullet 2 is 'travel to the nearest Fore Trap', which is the same zone you are already standing in; bullets 3 and 4 are check-then-check-again on the same object, the Divine Might Blank Target shape. Three rungs there would be three markers on one trap.

The Fore Trap gets no grid: the page names TWO of them, (H-5) via the River Murex from Veridical Conflux #02 and (J-12), and picking one would be a coin flip. Both are in the note. The marker rides the object name, which is what actually matters.

Bullet 4's sub-bullet is the good find: 'You will also obtain a [KI] Weakening trap fluid bottle, but you will have no indication of this.' No indication IN GAME -- the packet reports it fine, so it is exactly the kind of silent observable this schema exists for. The infusion distance mechanic (1/2/5 yalms, which sets the reward size) is not observable and is only a note.

'Resistance Sapper' is the same name in every Abyssea area, so every step keeps its zone.

steps.note: beside Veridical Conflux #00. Only one Ward Warden / Desert Rain / Crimson Carpet quest may be completed per Vana'dielian day in any Abyssea area, which nothing observable reports.

check it once to be told how far to stand, back off, then check it again to infuse. TWO traps exist and the page does not say which is nearest: (H-5), reached from Veridical Conflux #02 heading north through the River Murex, and (J-12) -- so no grid is recorded. 1 yalm is inside the fringe, 2 yalms just beside it, 5 yalms the maximum; accuracy sets the reward and is not observable. The bottle arrives with no in-game message.
the Cruor and Resistance Credits scale with how close you stood; the seal is a separate roll.

notes:
Four bullets, four steps, and the whole 'After the walkthrough: Notes' section is battle advice -- Carbuncle only, solo, 15 minute limit, buffs survive the level cap, pet food -- with not one step in it. I read it in full before deciding that.

The hard call is the zone of the Wind Protocrystal. The walkthrough never names it; the Description says the protocrystal is 'in Cape Teriggan' and Notes [6] calls the destination 'the Cloister'. Cape Teriggan is the zone you WALK to, not the zone the protocrystal stands in, so writing it would produce a marker that can never draw. 'Cloister of Gales' would be right and does resolve, but it appears nowhere on this page and I will not invent it. Zone is left null on steps 3 and 4: a null zone matches anywhere, and 'Wind Protocrystal' is a unique entity, so the marker still lands correctly and only the travel hint is lost.

Bullet 2 is optional. Trading the fork back to Rahi Fohlatti is a convenience teleport to the Cloister, not a gate -- you can walk to Cape Teriggan instead -- and Notes [6] says the teleport is one-shot while the fork can be re-obtained forever. It is on the same NPC as step 1, so the two share a marker regardless.

Repeatable is left false: the header says so, and Notes [6] offers a repeat of the FIGHT, not of the quest. Garuda and the Scroll of Instant Warp are header rewards and are not used as evidence.

STAGE D: quest confidence lowered high -> medium. The ladder survives every attack -- four bullets, four steps, source order, evidence obtained at the step that grants it and no reward used -- but half of it cannot say where it happens. The page names no zone for the arena, and its two location claims disagree: the Description puts the protocrystal 'in Cape Teriggan' while Notes [6] calls the destination 'the Cloister'. Steps 3 and 4 therefore carry a null zone, which is the honest record but leaves the ladder incomplete on a field the page should have supplied. Nothing is added to fix it -- 'Cloister of Gales' appears nowhere on the page. Medium is the confidence for a page that is unclear or incomplete.

steps.note: Summoner level 20 or higher; the fork is a normal inventory item, not a key item.

OPTIONAL convenience: trading the fork back sends you to the Cloister so you need not cross Cape Teriggan on foot. Notes [6] says the teleport is offered once -- a re-obtained fork buys another fight but no second ride. Prepare first; the page says to go whenever you are ready.

zone deliberately null -- the page calls this place only 'the Cloister' (Notes [6]) and puts the protocrystal 'in Cape Teriggan' (Description), which is the zone you travel THROUGH, not the one it stands in. See the quest note.
one-on-one and solo only, 15 minute limit. Notes say Carbuncle is the intended avatar (Siren works but do not use Clarsach Call, which Garuda absorbs); buffs applied outside survive the level cap.

notes:
Clean ten-bullet ladder with one real trap in it.

The trap: bullet 8 hands you the Map of the Attohwa Chasm the instant you zone into Boneyard Gully, which looks like textbook mid-quest evidence -- and it is not. The map is listed in the header's Reward, so by the reward rule it proves the quest is over rather than that the step is done, and it is doubly unusable because you only get it 'if you do not already own it'. A returning player would hold it from bullet 1 and the mark would jump straight to the end. Evidence is left null there and the Deed carries the ladder instead. (The item does not resolve against res/items.lua either, so nothing was lost.)

Zone folding: the wiki writes 'Bibiki Bay - Purgonorgo Isle', which is not a zone in res/zones.lua -- the isle is a second map of Bibiki Bay (id 4) and the Manaclipper is its own zone (id 3). Everything on the isle is therefore recorded as Bibiki Bay, and (H-9) is a grid on the isle map.

Bullets 3/4/5 are the standard examine-fight-examine on one ???: spawn the Peerifools, kill them, click again for the Deed. Bullet 10 is the page's own '(Optional)' closing dialogue and sits on the same NPC as bullet 9, so it costs nothing. Bullet 7's long sub-bullet is a route through the Maze of Shakhrami and stays a note.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 3: A ??? can never carry a marker; the rung is kept because the fight and the second click hang off it.

notes:
The whole quest is transacted with two DOORS, and the header does not say so. Start reads 'Yoran-Oran, Windurst Waters (S) (J-9) (Rhinostery)', but Yoran-Oran is never mentioned again on the page: bullet 1 says to examine the southern Rhinostery door, bullets 4 and 7 send you back to it, and bullets 5, 7 and 8 all transact with the Optistery door. Following the walkthrough over the header is the Blade of Evil / Carbuncle Debacle rule, so start is moved to the Rhinostery and the header string is kept verbatim in start.raw. This is a marker MOVE and a human can flip it back: if Yoran-Oran really does stand in Windurst Waters (S), his is the safer key.

The door names are recorded as the page writes them, 'Rhinostery' and 'Optistery', not as 'Door: X'. Windurst's stronghold entrances are named for the building, unlike San d'Oria's 'Door:Prince Royal's Rm'; v1's own quest_index already carries snpc='rhinostery' for a crystal_war quest, which is the closest thing to a live confirmation available at build time.

Grid conflict: header (J-9), bullet 1 (I-8) 'southern map'. (I-8) is used because it is the bullet giving the instruction; both are recorded. The Optistery is on the FIRST map at (F-8) -- two maps, two doors, easy to conflate.

'Quest Reqs: [KI] Bronze Ribbon of Service' has no slot in the schema -- gates carries fame, prev, level, jobs, repeatable and expansion, and none of them is a key item -- so it gates nothing here and is flagged. The name does not resolve against res/key_items.lua as written either. Bullet 8's one-game-day wait is merged into the final turn-in rather than made a rung of its own: it is the same door, and game time is invisible to the addon. Demoted to medium for the unmodellable prerequisite and the grid conflict, not because the ladder is in doubt.

steps.note: southern map. There are TWO Rhinostery doors and only the right-hand (south) one starts the quest. The header puts the giver at (J-9); the walkthrough puts the door at (I-8) and is followed. Checking it a second time repeats the directions and is not a step.

the lower levels of Giddeus -- plain Giddeus, not a (S) past version; the page says so and no such zone exists. The coin can be farmed or bought from the Auction House (Others > Beast-made). Talking to him before the trade is flavour only.
the same southern door; a second check just repeats the directions.
a different door on the FIRST map. They ask for a sheet of Vellum (craftable, or Auction House under Materials > Leathercraft) and the Lynx pelt key item.
first floor. This one IS the past version, spelled (S) on the page.
only the Vellum is traded -- key items cannot be -- but both must be held, so both are listed.

one full game day must pass after the Vellum trade before the Scroll of Retrace is handed over; game time is invisible to the addon. Same door as step 6, so one marker covers both. The scroll is the header Reward and is not evidence.

notes:
Thirteen bullets and a long, honest ladder across seven zones, with three key items and three separate evidence points, so the mark re-anchors well.

The four Giant Clams are a GROUP, not four rungs. They are all in Korroloka Tunnel but on four different maps, and the page's 'first / second / third / final' is a walking route from the Zeruhn Mines entrance, not a required order -- so all four draw at once, which is what a player actually wants when the clams are scattered over maps 1, 3, 5 and 2. Washu's flask is what you must hold at each; only the LAST group member carries the Flask of clam water, because the flask TURNS INTO the clam water once all four are done and duplicate evidence across a group would jump the mark inside it.

The header giver is Zoriboh but bullet 1 sends you to Rudolfo first, so Rudolfo is step 1 and Zoriboh step 2. Start stays on Zoriboh -- the marker for an unstarted quest should point at the person the header names -- and his (F-6) is recovered from bullet 2, since the Start field gives no grid.

'Quest Reqs: Promathia Mission 2-1' is a MISSION, not a quest, and there is no mission slot in gates. It is recorded in prev by title following the Divine Might precedent and flagged, because nothing downstream can match a mission title against the quest log.

Bullet 9 does not restate its zone; it inherits Port Bastok from bullet 8, and (F-5) beside Kagetora's (F-6) makes that read plainly. Bullet 7 (Gimb) is left with no items: the Storeroom key obviously travels with you, but the page never says what it opens, and asserting a hold requirement the page does not state is exactly the reaching this schema forbids. Bullets 11 and 12 are split because they are two zones -- the vortex is in Valkurm Dunes, the cutscene fires in Lufaise Meadows.

notes:
The sibling of Crimson Carpet II, and a shorter ladder because only one key item exists. Bullets 1 and 2 are one step -- bullet 2 is what bullet 1 gives you, a map Target marker and the Magicked flaxen sack -- and bullets 3 and 4 are one step for the same reason bullet 2 of Crimson Carpet is not its own rung: 'travel to the spot' is the same zone you are standing in, and the Repair Trunk is the thing you actually touch.

The destination has NO grid ref anywhere on the page. It is delivered as a marker on the player's own map, which the addon cannot read, so grid stays null and Veridical Conflux #06 goes in the note as the nearest fixed landmark. That is the honest answer; inventing a grid would put a marker in the wrong place.

The cramming minigame is not observable in any way. How much you pack sets the Cruor and Resistance Credits, over-packing tears the sack and FAILS the quest outright, and the sack's four condition messages are chat text. None of that can be a step or evidence, so step 2 carries no evidence at all and the ladder simply falls through to the turn-in.

The preamble line above bullet 1 -- one Ward Warden / Desert Rain / Crimson Carpet per Vana'dielian day across all of Abyssea -- is a cooldown, not a step. 'Resistance Sapper' is the same name in every Abyssea area, so every step keeps its zone.

steps.note: at Veridical Conflux #00. The sack and a Target marker on your map arrive together; the marker is not readable by the addon. One such quest per Vana'dielian day across all Abyssea areas.

the SMALLER of the Repair Trunks. No grid: the spot is given only as a map marker, with Veridical Conflux #06 nearby. Pack oil cloth, triangular flasks and elongated flasks -- more is more reward, but over-packing tears the sack and fails the quest. None of the four condition messages is observable.
choose 'Finish cramming' first. The seal chance is flat regardless of how much you packed; only the Cruor and Credits scale.

notes:
Nine bullets, seven steps, and three of the bullets are not actions at all.

Bullet 1 is parenthesised and is a precondition: one game day since the previous quest plus a re-zone into Aht Urhgan Whitegate. Neither is observable, so it folds into step 1 as a note. Bullet 3 is narration -- 'Raubahn will direct you to find and kill a Flan' -- delivered during Waoud's cutscene, with travel advice hanging off it; the page never sends you to Raubahn as a separate visit, so no rung is made for him. Bullet 6, 'You will be given a Sealed Immortal envelope', is the OUTCOME of bullet 5, so it becomes bullet 5's evidence rather than a step of its own. A verb scan would have produced three extra rungs there, one of them on an NPC you never walk to.

The header names the giver as 'Waoud/Raubahn'. Waoud is used, because bullet 2 says plainly 'Speak to Waoud to begin the quest' and Raubahn only appears inside the resulting scene; the header string is kept verbatim in start.raw.

Bullet 8's target is the honest loss. The page calls it 'the unnamed target by the pond at (H-7)' -- not a ???, not a named object, literally nameless -- so target is type none with a null name and that step keeps its ladder position and loses its marker. It sits in Aydeewa Subterrane, reached through Wajaom Woodlands; the bullet crosses three zones and only the last one is where the step happens.

'Repeatable: af' is the artifact-armour category leaking into the field and means false. 'Level: 50+ Blue Mage' is BOTH gates. The BC itself may be entered on any job -- the gate is on holding the quest, which the runtime only evaluates before you start, so it needs no modelling. Magus Charuqs is a header Reward and is not evidence. Medium overall for the Raubahn reading and the nameless target, not because the ladder is in doubt.

steps.note: as a Blue Mage. One game day must have passed since Beginnings and you must have re-zoned into Aht Urhgan Whitegate -- neither is observable. Raubahn gives the actual instruction inside this cutscene; the header lists him as a co-giver but the page never sends you to him.
in via the Home Point in Mount Zhayolm just outside the chamber, or a Mount Zhayolm Unity warp (level 128 or 135). Examining the gate opens the battlefield.
up to 18 players, and more players spawn MORE flans, so no count is recorded. Trust Magic is allowed and you need not be on Blue Mage to enter or clear it.
bullet 6 is the outcome of this conversation, not a step; the envelope is what it hands you.
second floor, inside the stall. The envelope is a key item and cannot literally be traded, but it must be held to deliver it.

the page calls it 'the unnamed target by the pond' and gives it no name at all, so it cannot carry a marker. Route: out of Aht Urhgan Whitegate by the (G/H-10) stairwell into Wajaom Woodlands, south to the Aydeewa Subterrane entrance at (K-9), then (H-7) inside the tunnel. Nothing aggros in there; the Phlebotomic Slug on the upper step can be pulled but will not.
Magus Charuqs and the Immortal Lion title; both are header rewards and neither is evidence.
